hardware.tested_state: read-only ESP32-S3 eFuse summary parsed through nSealr/esp32 security audit script

procedure: Sourced /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh in the same shell used for the audit.
Ran make IDF_PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodem1101 idf-audit-security-fuses from nSealr/esp32 revision 6886389.
The audit target invoked only espefuse.py --chip esp32s3 --port /dev/cu.usbmodem1101 summary through scripts/audit_security_fuses.py.
Recorded the parsed JSON blockers from the read-only eFuse summary.
expected_result: The development board should be auditable without burning eFuses, and the resulting JSON should keep irreversible production hardening gaps explicit before any signing claim.
observed_result: The read-only audit passed. The parsed eFuse state reported secure_boot_enabled false, flash_encryption_enabled false, download_mode_disabled false, manual_flash_encryption_download_disabled false, debug_access_locked false, and development_usb_jtag_available true. The production blockers were secure_boot, flash_encryption, debug_lock, download_mode, and manual_flash_encryption_download. raw_summary_sha256 was a796f1f81a324c5af0a3905eaa8d878b81fe348a6cbe4621178afc035fee1394.
limitations: This report is read-only eFuse posture evidence, not a firmware protocol smoke, display test, GPIO test, camera test, QR flow test, provisioning test, or real signing test.
The audit did not enable secure boot, enable flash encryption, disable download mode, disable manual flash-encryption download, or lock JTAG/USB debug access.
The observed state is appropriate for development bring-up only and is not a production custody profile.
sign_event remains signing_disabled until every production signing gate is satisfied.
